title: Evaluator implementation descriptor
description: File an evaluator implementation ships so a loader can install and run it with no code that knows that implementation by name. This is separate from the result descriptor in docs/evaluator-descriptor.md. See docs/implementation-descriptor.md.

format.description: The format stays /1. This version's kinds are integrity, advisory, and scenario. A later minor version widens the kind enum additively. A consumer MUST refuse a kind it does not know.

id.description: The evaluator.id this implementation writes on its results.

kind.description: integrity, advisory, or scenario. A later minor version widens this enum additively. A consumer MUST refuse a kind it does not know.

grading.description: integrity and advisory require none. scenario requires robot. Every other combination is rejected. At most one evaluator in a run may grade the robot. A descriptor is one evaluator, so the descriptor cannot state that rule. A consumer that loads a list of descriptors MUST refuse a list with two `grading` values of `robot`.

package.description: It installs from the descriptor's own repository at the same commit as the descriptor. The descriptor never names another source.

name.description: PEP 508 distribution name. A path, URL, git+ locator, or 40-character hexadecimal commit is rejected.

python.description: Fixed at 3.12 for now and will widen later.

module.description: Python module a loader runs with python -m.

arguments.description: Ordered arguments of the trial run. A top-level string may contain {evidence_manifest} and {result}, and may not contain {media_dir}, {world}, or {identity}. {result} is the path of one result file. integrity and advisory write that file. It is not a directory. {result_dir} is a directory a scenario run writes into. The per-trial result files in that directory are the results, and each one carries the declared result format. thresholds.json and any other file in the directory are not results. {result_dir} and {thresholds} may appear in a trial argument, including inside then, only when kind is scenario. integrity and advisory reject them. {media_dir} may appear only in a conditional whose if is media_dir, or in media.arguments. {world} and {identity} may appear only in media.arguments. {evidence_manifest} must appear in a top-level string. integrity and advisory must also include {result} there. scenario must include {result_dir} there. Conditionals do not nest.

media.description: The media run: a second process, used when this implementation grades recordings. integrity and advisory reject this key. A consumer runs the media run only when it has both a media directory and a world document; otherwise it runs no media process and writes no media result. The consumer substitutes {result_dir} separately from the trial run. `{result_dir}` is a directory a scenario run writes into. The per-trial result files in that directory are the results, and each one carries the declared result format. `thresholds.json` and any other file in the directory are not results. arguments is a flat list of strings. {evidence_manifest}, {media_dir}, and {result_dir} must each appear. {world} and {identity} may appear here. {identity} is the --identity string the media CLI records, stored as the evaluator input URI. Today's value is git+https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>@<commit>; the flag also accepts a commit or an image digest. Conditionals are not used: this object is already the media run.

module.description: Python module a loader runs with python -m for the media run.

exit_codes.description: Any exit code not listed in exit_codes is a failure with no result. Code 0 is required and means result.

result.description: `result` is `livingproof-evaluator-result/1.<minor>.<patch>`. Another major is refused. advisory names minor 1.3 or any later 1.x minor. A descriptor names the one version it writes. Consumers must check that the produced result's format equals the declared value and that its major is one they support.

argument.description: An argument string inside a conditional whose if is media_dir. The brace tokens it may contain are {evidence_manifest}, {media_dir}, {result}, {result_dir}, and {thresholds}. integrity and advisory reject {thresholds} and {result_dir}. scenario rejects {result}. NUL is rejected. A newline is allowed.

argument_without_media_dir.description: A top-level argument, or an argument in a conditional whose if is not media_dir. The brace tokens it may contain are {evidence_manifest}, {result}, {result_dir}, and {thresholds}. integrity and advisory reject {thresholds} and {result_dir}. scenario rejects {result}. It may not contain {media_dir}, {world}, or {identity}.

media_argument.description: An argument of the media run. The brace tokens it may contain are {evidence_manifest}, {media_dir}, {result_dir}, {world}, and {identity}. It may not contain {result}. NUL is rejected. A newline is allowed.

no_result.description: scenario rejects {result} in a top-level argument and inside then. {result} is the integrity and advisory result file.

no_result_dir.description: integrity and advisory reject {result_dir} in a top-level argument and inside then. {result} stays the path of one result file.

no_thresholds.description: integrity and advisory reject {thresholds} in a top-level argument and inside then.

conditional.description: Included only when the named input is present. then is a non-empty list of argument strings. Conditionals do not nest. {media_dir} may appear in then only when if is media_dir.
